Bug_Title: Assertions should not be used in production code
Bug_Details:
Assertions are intended to be used in test code, but not in production code. It is confusing, and might lead to ClassNotFoundException when the build tools only provide the required dependency in test scope.
In addition, assertions will throw a sub-class of Error : AssertionError , which should be avoided in production code.
This rule raises an issue when any assertion intended to be used in test is used in production code.
Supported frameworks:
JUnit FestAssert AssertJ
JUnit
FestAssert
AssertJ
Note: this does not apply for assert from Java itself or if the source code package name is related to tests (contains: test or assert or junit ).
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by using an assertion statement within the showBug method. This is not appropriate for production code as assertions can be disabled at runtime and their use can lead to confusion and potential ClassNotFoundException if dependencies are scoped only for testing.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug method with a negative value (-5), which triggers the assertion in the production code. Since assertions are not meant to be used in production code, this will cause the test to fail when assertions are enabled.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test run results indicate that the test passed without throwing an AssertionError, which means the assertion in the production code was not triggered during the test execution. This could be because assertions are disabled by default in Java, and they need to be explicitly enabled using the -ea JVM flag. Since the test did not fail, it does not confirm that the bug was triggered.
